quote_text:
What did you make of today? There's a lot of frustration and disappointment.  
I thought the first half—I don't think we turned  up, to be honest. You know, the team that have  
been as good as we've been in our last four league  fixtures—beating St Mirren, beating Dundee United,  
you know, should have got a positive  result against Rangers, and a draw against  
St Johnstone—that team never turned up in the  first half. Now, whether that was down to Hibs'  
reputation or whatever, but certainly we addressed  that at half-time and I thought when we came out  
in the second half, I thought we were the better  team. You know, and Marley Watkins coming on at  
left-back gives us a real positive in that area,  and I thought it was us looking like the team  
that were going to win the—sorry—to get the next  goal. So that's the team I want to see, that's the  
bravery I want to see. But then to allow the game  to slip and go away from us the way we did—the  
second, the third and the fourth goal—we need to  take real responsibility for it. It's happened too  
many times, so there's real disappointment from  that point of view. But you know what, I need to  
focus on what positives I can take from recent  performances and take them into the next five. 
You've mentioned the four good performances  before the game. This comes as a surprise to you? 
It does. It does a bit, you know, and that's  something that we need—as a group, we need to  
get to the bottom of. We need to make sure that—we  keep saying it—a consistent level of performance,  
you end up getting the results that you're looking  for from that. And that first-half performance—I  
thought we were a bit timid, you know, I thought  we were a bit on the back foot where we're not  
normally. You know, I thought our front three  didn't impact the game like they normally do. And,  
you know, it's a mistake we give away at  1–0. But, you know, if it's nothing each,  
it's one mistake that leads to their goal.  But second half I was really pleased with the  
response that we got. And as I say, I thought  we were the dominant team at that period of  
the game and we just need to get the goal. But  I need to stress as well that my frustration  
and disappointment comes from the manner of  the goals that we lose—second, third, fourth. 
In the next couple of weeks, it's about not  overreacting with this, but at the same time,  
you're stressing—that can't happen again. I think  so, yeah. I think there's a balance. And I think  
I've seen, at points, Hibs’ first half has to be a  reference point for us. That if we play that way,  
you know—and I reference the previous four  games—if we play that way, as opposed to  
the previous four games, then we'll give ourselves  problems that we don't need to give. Because we're  
a good enough team, you know. I'm really confident  in the team, I'm really confident in the players  
because of what I've seen previously. Today was  a surprise for me, I must admit. But then again,  
when I see the reaction that I get at the  start of the second half, that's the team  
that I want to see. And that's the team that will  be prominent from now to the end of the season. 
Is it a positive that it is so tight down there  that it's only going to take maybe a couple of  
good results and you bring yourself...? Yeah, I  think so. Because I think you've seen in recent  
weeks that we're more than capable of that. We're  more than capable of a level of performance.  
And I'm stressing that to the players—that we need  to make sure—sometimes it's a mindset. You know,  
we maybe came here, and as I say, on the back foot  a little bit because of Hibs' reputation, and I  
don't want my team to be that. You know, and I've  stressed that point. You know, we're a good side.  
You know, and when we do things properly, we're a  difficult team to play against and we're a strong  
team—you know, physically and in an attacking  sense. But today the disappointment was—and  
listen, we did chase the game a little bit,  you know, at 2–0 we put on subs and, you know,  
we tried to chase it a little bit. But as I say,  to lose the goals and the manner we lost them,  
you know, that's difficult to deal with. A couple of weeks until the next game. 
Tony Docherty: Absolutely, yeah. We just  need to keep working hard—smart. It's not  
really working hard at this stage of the  season, it's working smart. And you know,  
there's things again—we've seen already, we've  looked at the game in terms of the goals and some  
of the opportunities we presented to Hibs—that we  need to do better as a team. You know, and listen,  
I said at the very start of the game—teams keep a  clean sheet as a team. You don't look at just the  
defenders. It's the attacking players that can  help, the midfielders. The midfielders can help  
the defenders, that can help the goalkeepers.  So we're all in this together and we need  
to make sure that—as I say—a reference point  going forward. There's two reference points:  
our previous four performances, and that first  half against Hibs. And if, you know, we do one  
and not the other, we'll give ourselves a problem. Injury updates? Yeah, he was feeling his hamstring  
coming into the game. McGhee was the same.  Luke McCowan unfortunately felt his hamstring  
in training, you know, a recurrence of the injury  he picked up before the Rangers game. So again,  
we've picked up a few injuries. But you know  what, we'll dust ourselves down. As you say,  
we've got a couple of weeks to make sure  we prepare properly for the fixtures that  
are coming up. But it's important that we  focus on the positives and the previous  
references—the performances we put in prior to  this game. But we must learn from this game.
title: 'I was surprised' Tony Docherty Post Match Press Conference | Hibs 4-0 Dundee
